lines.formula: 1 month x K2,700.00 = K2,700.00, capped at the K1,757.48 due
lines.note: s.53(5): where an employee refuses to work the notice period, the employer may deduct, from money due on termination, what the employee would have earned in it. That is a deduction under a written law, so s.68(1)(a) allows it; s.79(c) makes any deduction outside s.68 an offence. s.69 is not the basis: it only bars deductions taken as a reward for providing or keeping a job. The set-off cannot exceed the money due on termination; anything beyond that is a debt the employer must claim, not a deduction.

flags.message: Whether s.53(5) reaches an employee who resigns without notice, rather than one who refuses to work a notice period the employer gave, is not settled by its text. A contract clause requiring notice or pay in lieu gives the employer a claim, but taking it from final pay still needs s.53(5): s.68(1) lists no other route.

flags.message: Gratuity runs to the last day of employment (15 Jan 2026), not to the last month end: it is computed on basic pay earned 'as at the effective date of termination' (s.54(1)(c)) or prorated 'in accordance with the period of employment' (s.73(2)).

Monthly wages K2,700.00 = basic K2,000.00 + allowances K700.00. Wages for part of a month are prorated by calendar days; gratuity and leave use basic pay only.

flags.message: Paying gratuity before the contract ends is not required, and the Code does not bar it: s.73(1) fixes when it falls due. Pay it as an advance against the gratuity, agreed in writing, and deduct it from the final figure. ZRA treats an advance against gratuity to an employee still in employment as exempt (ZRA Practice Note No. 1 of 2026, para 40). An advance is not a salary advance under s.68(1)(c), so it is settled against the gratuity, not recovered from wages.
